specializations.name: Product Film Direction
specializations.inputs: Product purpose, supported capabilities, audience, intended takeaway and permitted source material
specializations.decision: Choose the product change worth showing and the minimum sequence that makes it understandable. An input-process-result sequence is one option; a metaphor, direct comparison or quiet detail may fit better. Distinguish demonstrated behavior from illustrative condensation.
specializations.mechanism: A visible relationship between an action and a result can make the product message concrete.
specializations.tradeoff: An attractive simulation may imply an unsupported capability or spend its duration on interface detail instead of the benefit.
specializations.verification: Review the sequence without explanation. Compare each visible claim with supplied evidence; distinguish an illustration from functional validation. Check that the intended result can be identified.
specializations.output: Product beat plan with claim evidence, visual changes and editorial handoffs
practice: Specify the desired audience understanding per beat and the change that communicates it; omit redundant navigation.
Choose which interactions need continuity and which may be condensed with a clear editorial cut. Do not use a loading animation as proof of actual speed.
Send UI behavior to UI Choreography and state-to-state motion to Motion Choreography. Keep exact product identity and screen content in the project.
specializations.evidence: Authored transferable craft hypothesis; validate through actual project output and audience-relevant review.

specializations.name: UI Choreography
specializations.inputs: Component IDs and hierarchy, accurate UI content, action/state sequence and edit ranges
specializations.decision: Define causal state transitions and visible feedback before animating. Coordinate cursor, input, selection, menu, progress and result only when present in the brief. Preserve component anchors and nested coordinate spaces; use the existing layout and transform owners for implementation.
specializations.mechanism: Stable state relationships can let the viewer follow what changed and why.
specializations.tradeoff: Simultaneous changes can hide causality; simulated UI may misrepresent the product; excessive realism can bury the key idea.
specializations.verification: Check each state change against its trigger, panel anchors, text bounds, occlusion and reading interval. Inspect interruption and entry/exit boundaries; keep functional claims separate from the visual demo.
specializations.output: UI state/action map, component anchors, cue dependencies and motion handoffs
practice: Use states such as idle, input, selection, processing and result only when relevant; declare valid transitions and which parts persist.
Bind an event to the actual cue source. Use measured speech timing only when available; hand-authored editorial cues must be labeled.
Separate the panel transform from content reveals. Anchor menus to their control and preserve the connection through reframing.
Treat cursor blink, hover, focus, spinner and selection highlight as optional cues. Scope them to meaningful intervals rather than running every cue continuously.
specializations.evidence: Authored transferable craft hypothesis; validate through actual project output and audience-relevant review.

specializations.name: Motion Choreography
specializations.inputs: Intended change, stable object IDs, key states, hierarchy, timing constraints and optional cues
specializations.decision: Choose the primary action and dependent responses. Describe their relative timing, preserved relationships and attention handoff. Permit overlap, sequential movement, independent motion or stillness according to meaning; delegate trajectory, easing, springs and camera algorithms to their existing owners.
specializations.mechanism: Coordinating dependencies can make multiple moving parts read as one intentional action.
specializations.tradeoff: Moving everything together feels mechanical; excessive offsets fragment a single event; a universal beat grid can obscure meaning.
specializations.verification: Review whether the main action is identifiable and the next event begins with enough context. Inspect interrupted settling, pivots and handoffs. Use target-speed playback before claiming successful pacing.
specializations.output: Action dependency map with primary/supporting tracks, overlaps, holds and invariants
practice: Plan anticipation, travel, settle and reading states only where useful; specify which intervals may overlap.
Separate object, parent-group and camera changes so compounded transforms remain intentional.
Assign one owner to each driven property. Pass the motion endpoints and intended response to easing/secondary-motion; avoid competing drivers.
Re-evaluate relative timing after retiming or copy changes. Preserve deliberate silence and stillness as valid action choices.
specializations.evidence: Authored transferable craft hypothesis; validate through actual project output and audience-relevant review.

specializations.name: Attention Direction
specializations.inputs: Audience task, focal subjects, layout, motion tracks, reading needs and viewing scale
specializations.decision: Choose the intended focal event and how attention passes to the next one. Allocate movement, scale, contrast, depth and detail around that purpose. Keep competing accents subordinate when clarity is needed; permit distributed attention when intentionally required.
specializations.mechanism: Coordinated visual cues may help preserve an understandable sequence of attention.
specializations.tradeoff: Glow, camera motion or decorative highlights can attract attention away from meaning; focal intent is not proof of actual viewer gaze.
specializations.verification: At intended viewing size, review what can be understood on a first pass and inspect the busiest interval. Record reviewer observations as such; do not claim eye-tracking or audience retention without measurement.
specializations.output: Focal-event plan, attention handoff anchors and competing-salience corrections
practice: Declare an intended focus per relevant interval and an anchor connecting the next state; change the plan when the narrative needs a deliberate break.
Use empty space and stillness as available tools. Before adding blur, reduce competing contrast or motion if that solves the problem.
Keep defocus, motion blur and glow distinct; request the required operation from compositing/temporal-sampling instead of conflating them.
Try a different cue such as shape or position when a color correspondence is inaccessible, ambiguous or inconsistent with the project identity.
Coordinate caption hierarchy, framing and local look changes around the intended event. One salient layer may lead while the others hold; purposeful distributed attention is still allowed.

Use small-versus-large wording, negative space or a repeated phrase as possible attention relationships without adopting a source font or palette. Record intended focus as a design hypothesis, not measured gaze.
specializations.evidence: Authored craft hypothesis informed by multiple visual studies; sampled frames establish visible states, not validated audience response, playback rhythm or audiovisual synchronization.

handoffs.condition: When a product benefit or interaction is the subject
handoffs.payload: Intended takeaway, accurate claims and editorial ranges

handoffs.condition: When product meaning depends on interface behavior
handoffs.payload: Supported UI states, causal actions and result claims

handoffs.condition: When a product sequence is planned
handoffs.payload: Beat intentions, readable states and permitted condensation

handoffs.condition: When product beats require coordinated movement
handoffs.payload: Meaningful changes, state dependencies and continuity invariants

handoffs.condition: When multiple interface events depend on each other
handoffs.payload: Component hierarchy, factual labels, states and anchors

handoffs.condition: When state changes need coordinated visible action
handoffs.payload: Action/state map, persistent IDs, trigger relationships and holds

handoffs.condition: When panels or menus change over time
handoffs.payload: Timed component bounds, anchor relationships and protected text

handoffs.condition: When a UI sequence is constructed
handoffs.payload: Explicit state transitions, local times, component IDs and parameters

handoffs.condition: When action relationships need durations and overlaps
handoffs.payload: Primary/supporting actions, comprehension needs and boundary intent

handoffs.condition: When action tracks need transform evaluation
handoffs.payload: Stable IDs, endpoints, coordinate spaces, pivots and intended trajectories

handoffs.condition: When a track needs a movement character
handoffs.payload: Travel and settle intent, joins and permissible overshoot

handoffs.condition: When a part follows a primary driver
handoffs.payload: Driver identity, attachment, lag intent and interruption constraints

handoffs.condition: When a shared action bridges adjacent shots
handoffs.payload: Outgoing/incoming states, identity and overlap constraints

handoffs.condition: When multiple actions compete or hand off focus
handoffs.payload: Intended primary action, supporting tracks and event ranges

handoffs.condition: When composition must stage the focal event
handoffs.payload: Focal anchor, protected reading region and competing visual priorities

handoffs.condition: When framing changes are used to direct attention
handoffs.payload: Focal track, screen-space anchor and required readable intervals

handoffs.condition: When contrast, glow or blur mediates emphasis
handoffs.payload: Required legibility, focus intent and permitted optical treatment

handoffs.condition: When fast motion or blur threatens the focal content
handoffs.payload: Critical reading ranges, output scale and moving-edge needs

handoffs.condition: When a supplied lesson reveals transferable action relationships
handoffs.payload: Observed dependencies, study scope, uncertainty and alternative realizations

handoffs.condition: When a supplied lesson suggests an attention handoff
handoffs.payload: Observed composition changes and untested perceptual explanation

handoffs.condition: When a lesson concerns product storytelling
handoffs.payload: Observed sequence and claim limits, without importing source identity

handoffs.condition: When coordination, interruption or continuity fails
handoffs.payload: Observed issue, affected interval and intended event relationship

handoffs.condition: When important information is missed or visual competition dominates
handoffs.payload: Scoped reviewer observations and competing cue range

handoffs.condition: When a visual UI state is misleading or unreadable
handoffs.payload: Failed claim/layout condition and affected state transition

handoffs.condition: When a new comparison qualifies a learned relationship
handoffs.payload: Conflicting observation, comparison scope and revised conditions

handoffs.condition: When expressive caption emphasis competes with performance or framing
handoffs.payload: Caption role, intended semantic emphasis, protected subject events and reading ranges

handoffs.condition: When a caption group reveals, expands or spans reframing
handoffs.payload: Measured phrase/group bounds, local anchors, animated extremes and relevant time intervals

handoffs.condition: When language becomes an independent visual scene
handoffs.payload: Approved semantic groups, text role, emphasis spans and cue provenance

handoffs.condition: When an accent carries a semantic association
handoffs.payload: Meaningful spans, local accent role and required non-color correspondence

handoffs.condition: When expressive language uses an interface with dependent states
handoffs.payload: Illustrative state map, semantic mapping and screen/panel hierarchy

handoffs.condition: When spatial type or phrase groups change over time
handoffs.payload: Phrase anchors, measured final layout and projected intermediate bounds

handoffs.condition: When a scoped look change participates in an editorial emphasis
handoffs.payload: Intended focal event, treatment range and semantic purpose

handoffs.condition: When matching choices or deliberate look differences affect adjacent shots
handoffs.payload: Matched relationships, intended discontinuities and relevant source roles

handoffs.condition: When performance, text and imagery must share a focal event
handoffs.payload: Meaning changes, lead/support roles and proposed emphasis ranges

handoffs.condition: When an insert or montage bridges source changes
handoffs.payload: Insert role, provenance status, persistent phrase/motif and return anchor

handoffs.condition: When framing or inset footage changes around captions
handoffs.payload: Coordinate-space transforms, protected regions and caption anchoring intent

handoffs.condition: When measured phrase geometry is animated or reframed
handoffs.payload: Font/copy revision, semantic group, final bounds and local anchor

handoffs.condition: When text meaning, speaker or cue precision changes
handoffs.payload: Reviewed utterance, semantic span map and timing provenance

handoffs.condition: When a caption group collides or cannot reach a readable state
handoffs.payload: Affected group/time range, projected conflict and proposed reflow or restaging

handoffs.condition: When caption entry, carryover or exit hides meaning
handoffs.payload: Observed phrase issue, affected interval and actual inspection scope
